evidence: Enumerated every negative (refused / not offered / hidden / unchanged / not seen / not loaded again / does not leak) leg across all 47 criteria in the five judge.toml files and checked each for a matching success case. GATES: hro_gate_render (gates/render/judge.toml:23) pairs the wrong-password stay-signed-out leg with the correct-password sign-in, and render/prompt.md:9 calls it 'the required positive control'. hro_gate_shared has no negative leg. FUNCTIONAL (tests/scored/functional/judge.toml), each with an in-criterion control: hro_job_open:29 ('the successful opening is the control'); hro_add_email_rules:47 (same address on another job accepted); hro_move_one_stage:56 (one-stage forward/back work); hro_reject_reason:83 (reject with reason moves to Rejected); hro_reject_hired:92 ('A rejection of a non-hired card is the control'); hro_reopen:101 (reopen to own stage plus undo); hro_interview_full:110 ('the two cards that entered Interview are the control'); hro_undo_full:128 (undo with room 'the same-kind control'); hro_mgr_early_refused:155 ('their late-stage moves are the control'); hro_mgr_other_job:164 (own manager's move); hro_observer_readonly:173 (Rafael's identical successful requests); hro_candidate_no_staff:182 (candidate's own data loads plus Rafael's same-kind requests; zero if the candidate gets no data); hro_anonymous:191 (signed-in success of each); hro_stale_refused:200 (original successful move; F must be where Mei put it); hro_bulk_all_or_none:218 and hro_bulk_places:227 (successful multi-card moves / later two-card move); hro_undo_conflict:245 (undo after an unrelated change goes ahead); hro_undo_once:254 (successful undos); hro_activity_refusals:272 (successful actions' lines); hro_notes:281 (recruiter and own-manager notes succeed, Observer reads both); hro_msg_compose:308 (normal send); hro_unread_counts:335 (count rises by exactly two before the 'does not rise while open' and 'own messages never count' legs); hro_unread_scrolled_up:344 (notice appears within 15 s and read after he goes to it); hro_seen:353 (seen after Tomas/Bill/Rafael); hro_thread_access:362 (Rafael's send, Mei/Bill write); hro_drafts:371 (draft stays; other conversation keeps its own); hro_candidate_private:389 (own applications and messages load, Rafael's identical read succeeded; 'A candidate page that receives none of its own data is 0'); hro_restart:407 (data present after restart_app before 'not loaded again'). POLISH (tests/scored/polish/judge.toml): hro_pol_live_board:23 and hro_pol_live_thread:32 make the row 0 if the update never arrives, so a dead live feed cannot earn 'nothing was disturbed'; hro_pol_earlier_place:41 requires 'the earlier ones above it'; hro_pol_failed_send:50 requires the retry to be 'sent once'; hro_pol_session_resume:59 states the post-sign-in send is 'the positive control' and requires Rafael's drafts to return after Mei's empty view. VISUAL: likert craft only, no negative legs. PROMPT-LEVEL BACKSTOP: functional/prompt.md:13 'Every refusal row needs its own positive control: a successful action of the same kind, observed in this review'; prompt.md:17 requires role replays to send a current version and be otherwise legal, with Rafael's same fresh request as control, and says 'a refusal for a duplicate, a skip or a full stage does not count as the role refusal' and a stale/out-of-date refusal 'does not count as that rule's or role's refusal'. Together these block a refuse-everything or 409-everything app from earning role or rule refusals. In prompt.md:23 hidden controls are explicitly not enforcement: the server refusal must be observed by replay. The public rules support the exact-status negatives: hireops_rules.md:21 (401 for no session) and :23 (404 for a conversation the caller may not see). BROKEN-APP PROBES (reasoned, not run): (1) A refuse-every-write app fails the gate (constraints needs a UI-created job and candidate visible to the Observer), and every refusal row would also lose its in-criterion success control. (2) An app whose moves into Interview always fail with a hard-coded 'Interview full' message gets 0 on hro_interview_full because its control is that two cards entered. For hro_refused_put_back that app is caught only by the prompt-level rule at line 13 and because a correct 'reason' presupposes a really full Interview (A and B never enter). (3) An app whose Activity view is empty fails hro_activity_refusals through its control. (4) A dead load-earlier button fails hro_pol_earlier_place ('earlier ones above it'). CONFORMING ALTERNATIVE PROBE: an app that hides illegal controls (skip moves, Observer actions, reject on Hired) is not penalised. Each such row says 'hiding it is optional' / 'is the app's choice' and grades the server refusal by replay of an observed request. An app with no version field is not falsely failed: line 17 asks for the current version 'or freshness value' only where one is sent. I found no conforming app that a negative leg would fail. RESIDUAL WEAKNESSES (Note-level, P3): (a) hro_refused_put_back (functional/judge.toml:137) is a refusal-UX row with no control written into its own description. It relies on prompt.md:13 and on the L protocol's earlier 'move B into Interview (2 of 2)'. (b) hro_mgr_early_refused (:155) names 'their late-stage moves' as the control even for the open-job, add-candidate, Applied re-order and Screen-reopen legs, where the same-kind controls (Rafael's S open/add, M re-order, R 'as Rafael reopen it') come only from prompt.md:13/17 and the protocol, not from the criterion text. In both cases the global functional rule forces a same-kind observed control, so I did not find a broken app that would be credited. RISK: risk is set because this row's guarantee ('a totally broken app can't earn it') depends on the configured judge following the controls. raw-evidence-index.json states 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent'. The only runtime artifacts are scripted golden observations, which say nothing about weak or broken apps. No mutated or dead-feature app has been run through the configured judge, so judge adherence to the controls is unmeasured.
suggested_fix: Optional hardening (not a blocker): in hro_refused_put_back, add 'the two cards that entered Interview in L are the control'; in hro_mgr_early_refused, name Rafael's same-kind open-job, add-candidate, Applied re-order and reopen successes as the controls for those legs. Separately, record a configured-judge run on a dead-feature or refuse-everything mutant to measure that refusal rows score 0 without their controls.
